newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy ENEL chief against group break-up.
newsitem.headline: Italy ENEL chief against group break-up.

text.p: The managing director of Italy's state-owned electricity utility group ENEL Franco Tato said he is against government plans to split the company up ahead of ENEL's planned privatisation.

Tato told the Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Saturday that the division of ENEL would be an error, but industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said on Sunday that the government must press ahead with its plans.

Currently, a parliamentary commission headed by undersecretary at the industry ministry Umberto Carpi has put forward a plan to make ENEL into a holding company to control different operating companies within the whole ENEL group.
Two years ago, a plan was drawn up to divide the group into three operating companies covering energy production, transmission and distribution, but this was never followed up.

"On distribution, I do not see the advantages to consumers deriving from the break up of ENEL. Fragmentation will only push up costs. Stimulation of competition can come in other ways with international comparisons between companies in the sector," Tato said.

But industry minister Bersani was reported in La Repubblica newspaper on Sunday saying, "Tato must understand that his shareholder, that is the Treasury, has two problems. First is not to weaken the company and to do that it must get thinner, and second is to open the market to liberalisation."

Last month, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said that there were still several problems to solve before ENEL could be privatised, such as how to let in private operators and if it is possible to think of a plurality of producers and distributors, and all of these problems have yet to be addressed.
No date has been set for ENEL's privatisation, but Ciampi has said he wants to launch the privatisation of ENEL after the sale of state-controlled telecoms holding STET which is seen later this year.
